gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Warnes stretches out its letters in bold, spacious display strokes that taper off before they touch. Noto Sans Avestan is a plain sans with a tall x-height, and that gap in weight and attitude is the best thing about the pair.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Expressive, with letterforms that stay at exactly one stroke contrast, Warnes leads with wide-set spacing. Noto Sans Balinese follows in a plain sans with short ascenders and breathing room inside each curve, so the page moves from showy to settled.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Loud, stretched and stroke-flat. Noto Sans Bamum sits under Warnes as a plain sans with big open counters in its small letters, and that difference in weight is what the pair does best.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah:
Warnes draws its bold letters with a plain, unmodulated outline.

Noto Sans Bassa Vah has a dominant midsection and an open-jawed c, so the sans text feels compact and busy beside the heading's spread-out, tapering ink strokes.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-batak:
Noto Sans Batak towers with a tall x-height.

Warnes above it is bold and unit-width throughout, with stretched spacing, while the body's wide e never looks squeezed, so a long passage would feel open and approachable beneath that heading.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Expressive and bold, Warnes looks like glass tubing, hollow and constant in thickness, with tapering ink strokes that stop short of touching. Noto Sans Bengali answers in sans-serif with open mouths.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuki: Warnes keeps one line width through every curve and straight, with spaced-out, tapering ink strokes that never quite meet. Yet Noto Sans Bhaiksuki is the one built for reading, its swollen lowercase and open apertures being easy on the eye in sans-serif.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Noto Sans Brahmi is a sans with a high mean line and open-ended curves, which keeps it moving smoothly. A longer passage would glide along under Warnes.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-buginese: Warnes spreads its bold letters wide with no thin strokes, so nothing vanishes in the glare. And Noto Sans Buginese sits quietly beneath as a sans with short ascenders and open mouths like unjoined chalk arcs.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Noto Sans Buhid has generous space between its curve ends and the stem, plus a high-set x-height. But Warnes is where the pair's strength lies: every stroke carries the same visual weight, bold and stretched.
